question: What is the primary goal of individual diet planning?

options.A: Eliminating all carbohydrates from daily meals
options.B: Reducing food costs to the absolute minimum
options.C: Following a strict menu designed for the general public
options.D: Meeting nutritional needs while respecting personal preferences

explanation: Individual diet planning focuses on tailoring nutritional intake to match personal needs, health status, and lifestyle choices. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h1)

question: Why must a diet plan be tailored rather than generalized?

options.A: Standard public health messages are illegal to use in hospitals
options.B: Patients refuse to eat unless their exact recipes are provided
options.C: Every person has unique physiological states and daily routines
options.D: Generic menus always cause severe vitamin deficiencies

explanation: People differ in health status, activity levels, and financial situations, making personalized plans much more effective. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h1)

question: Which DRI value meets the nutrient requirements of nearly all healthy individuals?
explanation: The RDA is set high enough to cover the daily needs of nearly all healthy people in a specific life stage group. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h2)

question: When is an Adequate Intake (AI) used instead of an RDA?

options.A: When a patient is diagnosed with severe malnutrition
options.B: When scientific evidence is insufficient to set a definite RDA
options.C: When evaluating the exact calorie needs of athletes
options.D: When calculating the maximum safe dosage of a vitamin

explanation: An AI is established through observation when there is not enough solid data to calculate a precise RDA. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h2)

question: Anthropometric measurements in a nutrition assessment include which of the following?

options.A: Height, weight, and body mass index

explanation: Anthropometry involves physical body measurements such as height, weight, skinfold thickness, and BMI. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h3)

question: Why is relying solely on body weight misleading when assessing nutrition?

options.A: Body mass index is the only legally accepted clinical standard
options.B: Scales in clinical settings are rarely calibrated properly
options.C: Weight changes only occur over periods of many years
options.D: Normal weight individuals can still suffer from micronutrient deficiencies

explanation: Body weight tells us about mass and composition, but it reveals nothing about whether a person gets enough vitamins and minerals. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of visual food guides in diet planning?

options.A: Calculating the exact economic inflation rate of local markets
options.B: Translating abstract nutrient standards into everyday food choices
options.C: Determining the precise biochemical composition of proteins
options.D: Prescribing pharmaceutical vitamin supplements for patients

explanation: Food guides give patients simple pictures and categories to help them select real foods at the market. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h4)

question: A balanced plate model typically recommends filling half the space with which food groups?
explanation: Filling half the plate with fruits and vegetables ensures an adequate intake of vitamins, minerals, and dietary fiber. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h4)

question: A patient on a tight budget cannot afford imported salmon. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Tell the patient to skip protein entirely until they can afford salmon
options.B: Suggest affordable local protein sources like dried beans or local fish
options.C: Discharge the patient from nutrition counseling for non-compliance
options.D: Insist that they find extra money to buy the imported salmon

explanation: Practical diet planning adapts to the patient's financial reality by offering culturally appropriate, affordable alternatives. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h5)

question: Why do diet plans often fail when they ignore cultural food preferences?

options.A: Cultural foods automatically contain dangerous levels of sodium
options.B: Patients reject meals that clash with their traditions and tastes
options.C: Traditional recipes are scientifically proven to lack vitamins
options.D: Hospitals forbid patients from eating anything outside of formula

explanation: People eat what is familiar, comforting, and culturally acceptable; ignoring this leads to immediate plan abandonment. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h5)

question: Using a patient's hand to estimate food portions involves equating a palm size to which food group?
explanation: In standard visual portion estimation, the palm of the hand roughly corresponds to a single serving of meat or protein. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h6)

question: Why is spacing macronutrients evenly across daily meals important?

options.A: It guarantees rapid weight loss within forty-eight hours
options.B: It prevents the digestive system from ever resting
options.C: It helps stabilize energy levels and blood glucose
options.D: It eliminates the need to drink water during the day

explanation: Distributing food intake prevents sharp glucose spikes and crashes, maintaining steady energy throughout the day. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h6)

question: What is the first step when a patient fails to meet their dietary goals during follow-up?

options.A: Investigating the root cause of the non-adherence
options.B: Immediately doubling the prescribed medication dose
options.D: Scolding the patient for lacking self-discipline

explanation: Before changing a plan, the nurse must understand why it failed, such as checking for cost issues, boredom, or unrealistic targets. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h7)

question: Why should a diet plan be viewed as an ongoing cyclical process?

options.A: Health status, lifestyle, and goals change over time
options.B: Food prices fluctuate daily in the local markets
options.C: Government regulations require monthly menu rewrites
options.D: Patients get easily confused if recipes stay the same

explanation: As a person ages, encounters illness, or shifts activity levels, their nutritional needs and practical constraints evolve. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h7)
